Subject: SLO metrics definition and remedies — follow-up from demo

Hi Elaine — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: Agree a pragmatic SLO/SLA definition that covers streaming latency, concurrent session targets, and reporting cadence so you can finalize procurement.
- From the demo we heard: 95th percentile latency is most important for clinical workflows (real-time note generation), target ~300ms p95 for short prompts (<= 256 tokens). Burst tolerance for up to 200 concurrent streaming sessions is desired.
- Open questions we flagged: how you want "latency" measured for streaming responses (time-to-first-token vs. time-to-last-token), what qualifies as an SLA exclusion (retries, user network), and the concrete remedies you expect for breaches (service credits / termination rights).

Proposed next steps: 
1) We attach a short draft SLO clause that captures p50/p95/p99 measurement windows and a proposed exclusion list.
2) Can your team share a short load plan (we referenced a spreadsheet) and the preferred test harness so we can validate with a Guided PoC?
3) If the SLO language looks reasonable, we can surface it to Legal + Procurement and propose a 30-day staging SLA for the pilot.

I've attached a draft SLO clause and a load-test template. Suggest we sync again Thu 10:00am PT if that works — I can have Karthik on the call to walk the measurement specifics. 

Thanks,

Connor — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Measurement: For streaming use cases our priority is time-to-first-token (TTFT) for interactive UIs, but we also care about completion latency for background batch note generation. For the interactive flow we want p95 TTFT <= 300ms, and for batch completions p95 end-to-end <= 2s for payloads up to 1024 tokens.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming connections is our expected peak for combined front-end editors across three hospitals, but sustained concurrency will be closer to 80. We can test both sustained and burst profiles.
- Exclusions: We expect common exclusions — customer network outages, scheduled maintenance (with 48hr notice), and provider-side forced model updates — but we need to define allowed retry behavior (2 retries per request acceptable before counting as failure). Also want to confirm whether warm-up traffic during autoscaling is excluded.
- Remedies: Our procurement prefers service credits tied to monthly uptime / p95 violations and a limited right to terminate after 3 consecutive months of degraded SLOs. 

I'll distribute the internal load plan (ops@) and attach our internal test scenarios later today. Thu 10am PT works for a quick sync.

Best,
Elaine Tran
VP, Platform | MediSys Health

Subject: Re: SLO metrics definition and remedies — follow-up from demo

Elaine / Connor — thanks — a couple of technical notes so our SLO clause lines up with how we measure internally: 

1) Latency definition: Redwood measures TTFT as the delta between the request ingestion timestamp at the load-balancer and the timestamp when the first SSE chunk leaves the model worker (server-side). For non-streaming completions we measure request arrival -> last byte emitted. We can provide CSV telemetry for p50/p95/p99 windows with request IDs for 30 days.
2) Measurement windows: We report per-minute samples and aggregate to daily and monthly pXX numbers for SLA reporting. SLA violations are computed on the monthly aggregation.
3) Exclusions we propose to capture explicitly: customer network (ips we agree), scheduled maintenance windows (48hr notice), forceful model migration (when we need to evict capacity for security updates), and automated retry storms (we detect and mitigate). For warm-up/scale-up events we can exclude the first 10 minutes after autoscale if triggered by a deployment event; but sustained autoscaling events caused by legitimate traffic should not be excluded.
4) Remedies: Standard monthly service credit bands are fine (0.5x, 1.0x of monthly invoice for defined thresholds). Termination language: we prefer a remediation-first path with joint runbooks before termination; termination after 3 consecutive months is negotiable but we need objective triggers.

I can annotate the draft SLO PDF with our measurement language before Thu's call. Also proposing we run two guided load tests: (A) sustained 80 concurrent streams for 60 minutes, (B) burst ramp to 200 concurrent streams for 5 minutes repeated 3x. We'll then produce the p95/p99 telemetry and a short findings doc.

-Karthik
